title: When the entire Khalsa Panth had permitted the Nawab

blocks.text: Bhai Taru Singh replied that when the entire Khalsa Panth had permitted the act, he had no standing to oppose it. The prayer by the five devout Singhs, he said, would carry weight in the Divine Court, so the Nawab’s fate now rested on the authority of the Panth rather than on imperial power.

Subeg Singh took this assurance back to Lahore, where the terrified ruler dismissed his attendants and urgently asked for Bhai Taru Singh’s shoes to be brought. Once that symbolic submission was made, the urinary blockage got cleared, and the Nawab’s agony immediately subsided.

The narrative then broadens into a precedent from Kashmir, where tyranny and forced conversion had once ended in a ruler’s own humiliating affliction. That comparison makes the Nawab’s cure read not as a private miracle, but as part of a recurring moral pattern in the text.
